events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.living.FinalizeSpawnEvent - handler onEntitySpawn, @SubscribeEvent(priority = EventPriority.HIGH) at WitherSkeletonModule.java:75-76; the module subscribes itself to NeoForge.EVENT_BUS in onInitialize() at :58 (game bus, server only - the event is never fired on the logical client). The handler skips any spawn whose level is not a ServerLevel, which exempts the WorldGenRegion-based CHUNK_GENERATION path.

Vanilla claims below were read from the decompiled 1.21.1 sources the project compiles against (build/neoForm/neoFormJoined1.21.1-20240808.144430/steps/patchUserDev/output.jar) and NeoForge 21.1.248-sources.jar, not from memory.

1. THE BIG ONE - THE BLOCKING LOGIC IS INVERTED RELATIVE TO EVERY PIECE OF PROSE IN THE REPO.
   The class javadoc (:32-34), the shortDescription passed to super() (:49-50), the startup log line at :60 ("Normal skeletons are now banned from the Nether!") and README.md:49 all say "prevents normal skeletons from spawning in the Nether". The code does the opposite: skeletons in the open Nether are NEVER touched. WitherSkeletonModule.java:103 `if (allStructures.isEmpty()) { return; }` and :123 `if (!insideFortress) { return; }` mean the spawn is only cancelled when a fortress IS present. Real behaviour: plain skeletons are blocked ONLY in (Better-)Fortress-referenced chunks and spawn freely everywhere else in the Nether. The in-code comment at :113 ("Allow normal skeleton spawn inside Nether Fortress") and the debug log at :115 ("Allowed normal skeleton spawn inside Nether Fortress at {}") state the inverse of what happens eighteen lines later - that log line fires immediately before the spawn is cancelled. The broadcast text at :150 ("A normal skeleton tried to spawn in a Fortress but was blocked!") is the only prose in the repo that matches the code. A doc writer must decide whether to document the code or file this as a bug; do not copy the README sentence.

2. THE CODE IS LESS ABSURD THAN IT LOOKS - VANILLA FORTRESSES REALLY DO SPAWN PLAIN SKELETONS.
   NetherFortressStructure.FORTRESS_ENEMIES (NetherFortressStructure.java:17-23) is BLAZE w10, ZOMBIFIED_PIGLIN w5, WITHER_SKELETON w8, SKELETON w2, MAGMA_CUBE w3 - so ~7 % (2/28) of fortress monster spawns are plain skeletons in vanilla. Blocking exactly those and substituting a wither skeleton is a coherent design; only the prose describing it is wrong. Outside fortresses, skeletons are a normal part of Nether-wastes/soul-sand-valley spawning and the module leaves them alone.

3. THE MODULE'S FORTRESS GATE IS STRICTLY WIDER THAN THE REGION WHERE VANILLA'S FORTRESS SPAWN LIST APPLIES.
   serverLevel.structureManager().getAllStructuresAt(pos) (:101-102) is `level.getChunk(sec.x(), sec.z(), ChunkStatus.STRUCTURE_REFERENCES).getAllReferences()` (StructureManager.java:157-160) - the CHUNK's structure references, not a bounding-box or piece containment test. Vanilla, by contrast, only swaps in FORTRESS_ENEMIES when the mob category is MONSTER, the block below is NETHER_BRICKS and `getStructureAt(pos, FORTRESS).isValid()` (NaturalSpawner.isInNetherFortressBounds, :317-324), and the fortress spawn override is registered with BoundingBoxType.PIECE (Structures.java:176), i.e. ChunkGenerator.getMobsAt uses structureHasPieceAt (ChunkGenerator.java:442-459). Consequence: a skeleton that rolls out of the ordinary biome spawn list while standing in open lava, on netherrack, anywhere in a fortress-REFERENCED chunk is blocked and converted too, even though vanilla never intended it as a fortress spawn.
   Accepted structures: vanilla NetherFortressStructure (instanceof) OR any structure whose registry key is betterfortresses:fortress (:110-112).

4. "OPTIONALLY replaces them with Wither Skeletons" (README.md:49) is wrong - the replacement at :139 is unconditional. There is no config switch for it, and none for the message either; the class javadoc's "Configurable message format and replacement behavior" (:40) describes config that does not exist. WitherSkeletonConfig.buildModuleSpecificConfig is an empty method with the comment "No module-specific configuration needed", so WitherSkeletonConfig is a pure no-op subclass - the module could equally use AbstractModuleConfig.createDefault. The only keys in the file are the framework's own `enabled` and `debug_logging` (AbstractModuleConfig.java:58-66), which are excluded from configKeys by convention -> configKeys is genuinely empty.

5. THE BROADCAST IS GATED ON DEBUG LOGGING. broadcastSkeletonBlockedMessage returns immediately unless getConfig().shouldDebugLog() (:146). debug_logging defaults to AUTO (AbstractModuleConfig.java:66), which falls through to ModulesConfig.isGlobalDebugLoggingEnabled(), whose `globalDebugLogging` defaults to false (ModulesConfig.java:63, and :121 for the standalone spec). Out of the box nobody ever sees a chat message - the blocking and the replacement happen completely silently. README's "in debug mode" is accurate here; the shortDescription's unqualified "broadcasts messages about blocked spawns" is not. Once it does get that far the method also emits an UNCONDITIONAL INFO log line (:168) per blocked spawn, on top of the DEBUG lines at :129 and :194-196.

6. THE CHAT MESSAGE IS HARDCODED ENGLISH WITH EMOJI (:149-150) - no lang key exists (grep for "wither" over assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/en_us.json and over all of src/main/resources returns nothing), so it is not translatable. The coordinate line carries a ClickEvent RUN_COMMAND "/tp @p x y z" (:155-160); a non-op player clicking it gets a permission error, since /tp is permission level 2. The message goes to EVERY player on the server (:164-166), not just nearby ones.

7. ONLY PLAIN SKELETONS ARE AFFECTED. The check is `instanceof Skeleton` (:87). Verified against the decompiled 1.21.1 sources: Skeleton, Stray, Bogged and WitherSkeleton all extend AbstractSkeleton directly (Skeleton.java:15, Stray.java:20, Bogged.java:34, WitherSkeleton.java:28), so none of the other three match - strays and boggeds are untouched and the replacement wither skeleton cannot re-trigger the handler.

8. CHUNK-GENERATION SPAWNS ARE SILENTLY EXEMPT (missed by the first survey). FinalizeSpawnEvent.getLevel() returns a ServerLevelAccessor (MobSpawnEvent.java:62), and the module bails at :92 unless it is a ServerLevel. NaturalSpawner.spawnMobsForChunkGeneration takes a ServerLevelAccessor (NaturalSpawner.java:347) and is driven with a WorldGenRegion, so skeletons placed with MobSpawnType.CHUNK_GENERATION (NaturalSpawner.java:399-403) are NOT blocked. Everything that runs against a real ServerLevel is covered - normal mob-cap spawning (NaturalSpawner.java:196), mob spawners (BaseSpawner.java:161), spawn eggs and EntityType.spawn (EntityType.java:987), /summon (SummonCommand.java:95). The module applies no MobSpawnType filter of its own.

9. THE CLIENT-SIDE GUARD AT :82 IS DEAD CODE. FinalizeSpawnEvent's javadoc states it "is fired on NeoForge#EVENT_BUS, and is only fired on the logical server" (FinalizeSpawnEvent.java:35); WorldGenRegion.isClientSide() is false as well. The check can never fire.

10. THE REPLACEMENT BYPASSES EVERY OTHER SPAWN HOOK. replaceWithWitherSkeleton (:174-202) builds the mob by hand: EntityType.WITHER_SKELETON.create(level) (:177), moveTo (:184-185), finalizeSpawn (:188-189), level.addFreshEntity (:192). NeoForge injects FinalizeSpawnEvent into vanilla's finalizeSpawn CALL SITES via a transformer, not into Mob#finalizeSpawn itself ("this event is injected by a transformer and not via patch... it is not source-visible", FinalizeSpawnEvent.java:30, fired via EventHooks.onFinalizeSpawn) - so calling finalizeSpawn from mod code does not fire the event, and no other mod's spawn handlers, no spawn-placement rules and no mob-cap accounting see the replacement. The whole block is wrapped in catch(Exception) + logger.error (:199-201), and a null create() only warns (:178-181), so a failed replacement is near-silent; the original skeleton stays cancelled either way. Note also that the module calls event.setSpawnCancelled(true) (:133) and does NOT cancel the event, so vanilla still runs finalizeSpawn on the doomed skeleton before NeoForge drops it.

11. HISTORY / SCOPE CHANGE: the module used to also grant wither skeletons extra drops (golden apple 40 %, netherite scrap 10 %, skull 15 % - CHANGELOG.md:1362). Release 0.12.0 (commit dbc4787, "release: 0.12.0", 2026-05-10) stripped that out - CHANGELOG.md:1296 "WitherSkeletonModule: Zusaetzliche Drop-Logik entfernt; Drop-Konfiguration in das neue `mob_drops`-Modul verschoben." Those drops now live in the mob_drops module and are documented in docs/modules/mob_drops.md:31-33 (the skull is 12.5 % there, not 15 %). Do not attribute wither skeleton drops to this module.

12. NO DOCS PAGE. docs/modules/ has no wither_skeleton.md and README.md:48-49 carries no docs link, unlike most sibling modules.

13. FOOTPRINT: two source files in the module plus the standalone entrypoint. No mixins (no mixin/wither_skeleton/ package; grep for "wither" in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json returns nothing), no DeferredRegister/DeferredHolder/KeyMapping/RegisterCommandsEvent/CustomPacketPayload/@JeiPlugin anywhere in the module or its standalone class, no compat/ directory, no ModList.isLoaded, no assets and no data files (find over src/main/resources for *wither* returns nothing), no recipes, no loot tables. Nothing overrides shouldInitialize(), isEnabledByDefault() or isConfigurable(), so the defaults apply (Module.java:73-75 -> enabled by default true, consumed by ModulesConfig.java:87/:137 and ModuleManager.java:69; AbstractModule.java:112 -> shouldInitialize true). No TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK markers.

14. ENABLE GATE DIFFERS BETWEEN BUNDLE AND STANDALONE JAR (framework-wide pattern). onInitialize (:56-61) subscribes to NeoForge.EVENT_BUS unconditionally and isModuleEnabled() is only consulted at the top of the handler (:77-79). In the bundle, ModuleManager only calls initialize() for modules enabled at startup, so a runtime enable needs a restart while a runtime disable takes effect at once; in the standalone jar StandaloneModuleBootstrap boots the module unconditionally, so both directions work live.

15. HISTORY BASELINE: `git log --follow` on WitherSkeletonModule.java terminates at 441f105 "Add WitherSkeletonModule - prevents normal skeletons in Nether" (2025-10-07 12:31), which is also the only commit that ever added a file named WitherSkeletonModule.java anywhere in the repo (git log --all --diff-filter=A). git describe --contains puts it at v0.1.0~12, and v0.1.0 (2025-10-07) is the earliest tag by creatordate - so sinceVersion v0.1.0 is confirmed. Beware that `git tag --sort=version:refname` lists the unprefixed tags 0.6.0/0.9.0 first; sort by creatordate instead.
oneLiner: In chunks that belong to a Nether fortress (vanilla or Better Fortresses), a plain skeleton about to spawn is blocked and a wither skeleton takes its place - the rest of the Nether is left completely alone, despite what the README says.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Its structure `betterfortresses:fortress` is accepted as a fortress alongside the vanilla NetherFortressStructure, so the skeleton block/replacement also applies inside Better Fortresses structures. Matched purely by ResourceLocation against the structure registry - no ModList.isLoaded check, no compile dependency, no compat class, and the module works fine without the mod (only vanilla fortresses count then). Note this only decides where the module ACTS; vanilla's own fortress spawn list (NetherFortressStructure.FORTRESS_ENEMIES) is keyed to BuiltinStructures.FORTRESS and does not apply to the Better Fortresses structure unless that mod ships its own spawnOverrides.

shortDescription: Prevents normal skeletons from spawning in the Nether and broadcasts messages about blocked spawns
